questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a destination with interesting nature and a University with interesting subject relevant to my specialization.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The university had sent a lot of material before arrival and at arrival there was a whole week to sort everything out with registering for courses and settle in.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any, but if I needed it I could have contacted the study abroad officer.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You could either live in an apartment with 2-5 other people or in a dorm.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: At the dorms there were shared kitchens with everyone and in the apartments there were also a kitchen to share. In both dorms and kitchens you had to buy all utensils yourself, there were no pots and pans for cooking.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That you need to buy all kitchen utensils yourself and also all bedding yourself on arrival (pillow, duvet, sheets etc.). Also the student housing is a but more expensive than living in a shared house outside of campus, so it is worthwhile exploring other options.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was lucky to end up in an apartment with only 2 other students, so that was nice and they already had all kitchen utensils, so the only thing I had to buy was bedding.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before arriving I had to choose my subjects. There was a pretty good description of all subjects on the university website. As an exchange student I did not have access to the online registration portal before arrival. At arrival there was plenty of information on how to navigate the online portal if I wanted to change my courses or contact my professors.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a study abroad officer available to help and you could also go to the library to get help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful. I got almost all the courses I wanted except one, because it clashed with another course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is no need to stress about registering for classes. When you arrive you have a whole week to register and you have I think almost a whole month where you can change your courses if you don't like them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two 3rd year BA courses and two MA courses. I felt that all courses were a good level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Instead of just one exam in the end of the semester your final grade is based on assignments throughout the semester. Some courses might have a final exam, but your whole grade will no depend on it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Behavioural and Evolutionary Ecology, Antarctic Ecology, Molecular Marine Ecology, and Marine Predator Diversity and Ecology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Antarctic Ecology was very interesting, it had both some practical elements and some theoretical elements. All of the courses had a lot of practical elements.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The local public transport is non existing outside of Hobart, therefore if you want to see anything you will have to wither rent a car or buy a car. I, together with other exchange students, rented a car in the weekends to be able to see Tasmania.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is pretty much the same price as in Denmark and housing as well. There were a lot of free food given by the university each week, so if you wanted to you could spend very little money on food.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many cool clubs. Some nice clubs were diving, hiking, climbing, rafting and dancing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The hiking club was very cool. Many of the clubs did trips around Tasmania in the weekends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely go out into the national parks and enjoy the beautiful pristine nature. The east coast of Tasmania is very beautiful and accessible by car.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Tasmanians are very welcoming and open. They also seem to be very interested in other cultures.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openness and their love of nature. Many Tasmanians or people who live in Tasmania are very into camping, fishing, and hiking - and they were very keen to take you if you befriended them.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to UTAS if you want to go to a university that is very close to beautiful and unique nature. Do not expect a thriving night life in Hobart. See if you can find accommodation off campus.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Tasmania is a beautiful place and not as touristy as many other places in Australia, so it is a very authentic destination.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The openness and welcoming nature of Tasmanians.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To keep up with assignments.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
